4.official_text: Where any law provides that information or any other matter shall be in writing or in the typewritten or printed form, then, notwithstanding anything contained in such law, such requirement shall be deemed to have been satisfied if such information or matter is— (a) rendered or made available in an electronic form; and (b) accessible so as to be usable for a subsequent reference.
4.simplified_explanation: Grants complete legal recognition to digital records and electronic documents, establishing that electronic versions (such as via DigiLocker or mParivahan) satisfy legal requirements for physical paper documents.
4.applicability_notes: Directly applies when enforcement officials or authorities refuse to accept legally recognized digital credentials on government applications.

43.official_section_title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.
43.official_text: If any person without permission of the owner or any other person who is incharge of a computer, computer system or computer network, — (a) accesses or secures access to such computer, computer system or computer network or computer resource... (b) downloads, copies or extracts any data, computer data base or information... (i) destroys, deletes or alters any information residing in a computer resource or diminishes its value or utility or affects it injuriously by any means... he shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.
43.simplified_explanation: Imposes civil liability and financial compensation on anyone who accesses another person's device, account, or network without authorization, steals data, or introduces disruptive software.
43.applicability_notes: Applies to unauthorized account access, SIM swapping disrupting network connectivity, predatory loan apps extracting contacts, and remote screen-sharing tools installed deceitfully.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

43a.official_section_title: Compensation for failure to protect data
43a.official_text: Where a body corporate, possessing, dealing or handling any sensitive personal data or information in a computer resource which it owns, controls or operates, is negligent in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices and procedures and thereby causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain to any person, such body corporate shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person so affected.
43a.simplified_explanation: Requires companies, banks, and online platforms to pay compensation to affected citizens if they fail to implement reasonable cybersecurity safeguards resulting in the leak or theft of sensitive personal or financial data.
43a.applicability_notes: Directly relevant where a citizen suffers financial fraud or identity theft due to a data breach at a bank, telecom company, or e-commerce platform.

66.official_text: If any person, dishonestly or fraudulently, does any act referred to in section 43, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees or with both.
66.simplified_explanation: Converts unauthorized computer access, device hacking, and malicious data altering into a criminal offence punishable by up to 3 years imprisonment and fine up to five lakh rupees.
66.applicability_notes: General penal section for unauthorized digital account access, password tampering, email breaches, and malware/ransomware deployment.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

66b.official_section_title: Punishment for dishonestly receiving stolen computer resource or communication device
66b.official_text: Whoever dishonestly receive or retains any stolen computer resource or communication device knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen computer resource or communication device, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to rupees one lakh or with both.
66b.simplified_explanation: Punishes buying, receiving, or possessing stolen phones, laptops, or hacked computer databases with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine.
66b.applicability_notes: Applies to stolen smartphones used for fraudulent transactions, receiving leaked identity databases, and purchasing stolen digital devices.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

66c.official_text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh.
66c.simplified_explanation: Punishes fraudulently using another person's password, OTP, digital signature, biometrics, or personal identifiers with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine.
66c.applicability_notes: Primary penal section for OTP theft, card credential phishing, unauthorized SIM swaps, and fraudulent loans/SIMs taken using stolen Aadhaar/PAN cards.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

66d.official_section_title: Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource
66d.official_text: Whoever, by means for any communication device or computer resource cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
66d.simplified_explanation: Punishes cheating by impersonating someone else using a phone, computer, or digital communication. Punishable by up to 3 years imprisonment and fine.
66d.applicability_notes: Core penal section for digital arrest scams, bank customer service impersonation, task/job fraud, fake customs calls, romance scams, and fake lottery frauds.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

66e.official_text: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with fine not exceeding two lakh rupees, or with both.
66e.simplified_explanation: Punishes capturing, transmitting, or publishing photos or videos of private body parts without consent with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine up to two lakh rupees.
66e.applicability_notes: Applies to sextortion, non-consensual image distribution, and morphing of photos obtained from social media or predatory loan apps.

67.official_section_title: Punishment for publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form
67.official_text: Whoever publishes or transmits or causes to be published or transmitted in the electronic form, any material which is lascivious or appeals to the prurient interest or if its effect is such as to tend to deprave and corrupt persons who are likely, having regard to all relevant circumstances, to read, see or hear the matter contained or embodied in it, shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees...
67.simplified_explanation: Punishes publishing or transmitting sexually explicit or obscene material in electronic form with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine up to five lakh rupees for first conviction.
67.applicability_notes: Directly invoked in sextortion cases where blackmailers transmit or threaten to circulate compromising video recordings or morphed explicit material.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

67a.official_section_title: Punishment for publishing or transmitting of material containing sexually explicit act, etc., in electronic form
67a.official_text: Whoever publishes or transmits or causes to be published or transmitted in the electronic form any material which contains sexually explicit act or conduct shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees...
67a.simplified_explanation: Provides severe criminal punishment of up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to ten lakh rupees for publishing or transmitting electronic material containing sexually explicit acts.
67a.applicability_notes: Directly applies to aggravated sextortion blackmail involving transmission or leaking of explicit sexual video recordings or deepfake pornography.

72a.official_section_title: Punishment for disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract
72a.official_text: Save as otherwise provided in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, any person including an intermediary who, while providing services under the terms of lawful contract, has secured access to any material containing personal information about another person, with the intent to cause or knowing that he is likely to cause wrongful loss or wrongful gain discloses, without the consent of the person concerned, or in breach of the lawful contract, such material to any other person, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine which may extend to five lakh rupees, or with both.
72a.simplified_explanation: Penalizes employees, service providers, or telecom staff who access personal information under a contract and leak or sell it to unauthorized third parties without customer consent.
72a.applicability_notes: Directly applies to insider corporate data leaks, telecom staff selling call detail records (CDRs), customer KYC leaks, and BPO agent credential trafficking.

buds_act_2019.official_act_name: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019

3.official_text: On and from the date of commencement of this Act,— (a) the Unregulated Deposit Schemes shall be banned; and (b) no deposit taker shall, directly or indirectly, promote, operate, issue any advertisement soliciting participation in or enrol members in any Unregulated Deposit Scheme.
3.simplified_explanation: Completely bans any scheme that solicits deposits or investments with promises of returns without being registered with a statutory financial regulator like RBI or SEBI.
3.applicability_notes: Primary statutory ban against fake crypto trading platforms, multi-level marketing investment schemes, and task-based return schemes promising guaranteed daily earnings.
3.citation: Section 3, Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019

2_10.official_text: "defect" means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods or product and the expression "defective" shall be construed accordingly;
2_10.simplified_explanation: Defines what legally counts as a defect in goods: any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in quality, quantity, purity, or promised standard.
2_10.applicability_notes: Essential definition for all defective product complaints where a purchased item does not work, is damaged, or falls below advertised specifications.

2_11.official_text: "deficiency" means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service...
2_11.simplified_explanation: Defines deficiency in services: any failure, delay, negligence, or inadequacy in how a service is performed compared to statutory requirements or contractual promises.
2_11.applicability_notes: Applies to complaints regarding airlines, telecom operators, hotels, courier services, banking services, housing construction, medical care, and coaching services.

2_28.official_text: "misleading advertisement" in relation to any product or service, means an advertisement, which— (i) falsely describes such product or service; or (ii) gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality of such product or service; or (iii) conveys an express or implied representation which, if made by the manufacturer or seller or service provider thereof, would constitute an unfair trade practice; or (iv) deliberately conceals important information;
2_28.simplified_explanation: Defines misleading advertisements: ads that falsely describe products, give fake guarantees, mislead about ingredients/performance, or conceal critical information.
2_28.applicability_notes: Relevant when a consumer buys goods or services based on deceptive promotional campaigns, exaggerated performance claims, or hidden conditions.

2_42.official_text: "service" means service of any description which is made available to potential users and includes, but not limited to, the provision of facilities in connection with banking, financing, insurance, transport, processing, supply of electrical or other energy, telecom, boarding or lodging or both, housing construction, entertainment, amusement or the purveying of news or other information, but does not include the rendering of any service free of charge or under a contract of personal service;
2_42.simplified_explanation: Expressly brings banking, insurance, transportation (airlines/railways), housing construction, and telecom services under consumer law protection.
2_42.applicability_notes: Key statutory basis confirming that delays in home possession by builders, insurance claim repudiations, and airline flight cancellations are consumer service disputes.

2_47.official_text: "unfair trade practice" means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice including... falsely representing that goods are of a particular standard, quality, quantity, grade, composition, style or model... refusing to issue a bill or cash memo... refusing to take back defective goods or refund the amount paid... disclosing to other persons any personal information given in confidence...
2_47.simplified_explanation: Defines unfair commercial practices including refusing refunds for defective goods within promised periods, refusing cash memos, drip pricing, and deceptive sales pitches.
2_47.applicability_notes: Primary statutory basis for refund refusal cases, hidden charges, dark patterns, arbitrary cancellation fees, and coaching center fee retention.

21.official_section_title: Power of Central Authority to issue directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements
21.official_text: Where the Central Authority is satisfied after an investigation that any advertisement is false or misleading and is prejudicial to the interest of any consumer or is in contravention of consumer rights, it may, by order, issue directions to the concerned trader or manufacturer or endorser or advertiser or publisher to discontinue such advertisement or to modify the same in such manner as may be specified...
21.simplified_explanation: Empowers the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to investigate, ban misleading advertisements, and impose penalties up to ten lakh rupees on manufacturers and endorsers.
21.applicability_notes: Empowers regulatory action against systematic deceptive advertising campaigns, influencer endorsements without disclosures, and surrogate marketing.

35.official_section_title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
35.official_text: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by— (a) the consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or such service is provided or agreed to be provided; (b) any recognised consumer association...
35.simplified_explanation: Outlines how any citizen or consumer association can formally lodge a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (or online via e-Daakhil).
35.applicability_notes: The standard dispute resolution procedure across all consumer grievances when formal legal redress or compensation is sought from the Consumer Commission.

84.official_text: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the product contains a manufacturing defect; or (b) the product is defective in design; or (c) there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications; or (d) the product does not conform to the express warranty; or (e) the product fails to contain adequate instructions of correct usage to prevent any harm or any warning regarding improper or incorrect usage.
84.simplified_explanation: Holds manufacturers legally liable for compensation if a product causes harm, loss, or injury due to manufacturing defects, design flaws, or breach of express warranty.
84.applicability_notes: Directly applies where an electronic appliance, vehicle, machinery, or consumable product has manufacturing defects or fails to honor warranty obligations.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

85.official_section_title: Liability of product service provider or product seller
85.official_text: A product seller who is not a product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) he has exercised substantial control over the designing, testing, manufacturing, packaging or labelling of a product; or (b) he has altered or modified the product and such alteration or modification was the substantial factor in causing the harm; or (c) he has made an express warranty of a product independent of any express warranty made by a manufacturer and such product failed to conform to such warranty...
85.simplified_explanation: Holds product sellers and e-commerce platforms liable under product liability if they gave independent warranties, modified goods, or failed to pass on manufacturer warnings.
85.applicability_notes: Applies where an e-commerce marketplace or local dealer independently promised a warranty or modified the product before delivery.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

86.official_text: A product service provider shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the service provided by him was faulty or imperfect or deficient or inadequate in quality, nature or manner of performance which is required to be provided by or under any law for the time being in force, or pursuant to a contract or otherwise; or (b) there was an act of omission or commission or negligence or conscious withholding of any information which caused harm; or (c) the service provider did not issue adequate instructions or warnings to prevent any harm; or (d) the service did not conform to express warranty or the terms and conditions of the contract.
86.simplified_explanation: Holds service providers (such as authorized repair centers, technicians, installation agencies) legally accountable if their service is deficient or fails to conform to warranty terms.
86.applicability_notes: Directly relevant where an authorized repair center refuses warranty service, botches a repair, or withholds service promised under warranty.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

90.official_section_title: Punishment for manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing, or importing products containing adulterant
90.official_text: Whoever, by himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures for sale, or stores, or sells, or distributes, or imports any product containing an adulterant which is not injurious to health, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees; if causing injury not amounting to grievous hurt, imprisonment up to one year and fine up to three lakh rupees; if causing grievous hurt, imprisonment up to seven years and fine up to five lakh rupees; if causing death, imprisonment not less than seven years which may extend to life imprisonment...
90.simplified_explanation: Imposes criminal imprisonment and fines on traders, sellers, or distributors who sell expired, adulterated, or counterfeit goods.
90.applicability_notes: Applicable when a consumer is sold fake cosmetic/pharma products, expired groceries, adulterated food, or counterfeit branded items.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

18.official_section_title: Powers and functions of Central Authority
18.official_text: (1) The Central Authority shall— (a) protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class, and prevent violation of consumers rights under this Act; (b) prevent unfair trade practices and ensure that no person engages in unfair trade practices; (c) ensure that no false or misleading advertisement is made of any goods or services which is prejudicial to the interests of consumers or is in contravention of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder; (d) ensure that no person takes part in the publication of any advertisement which is false or misleading...
18.simplified_explanation: Vests the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) with regulatory powers to investigate consumer rights violations, mandate product recalls, order refunds, and penalize deceptive practices.
18.applicability_notes: Key regulatory mechanism when challenging systemic commercial scams, deceptive educational bootcamps, and widespread consumer exploitation.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

89.official_section_title: Punishment for false or misleading advertisement
89.official_text: Any manufacturer or service provider who causes a false or misleading advertisement to be made which is prejudicial to the interest of consumers shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees; and for every subsequent offence, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to fifty lakh rupees.
89.simplified_explanation: Imposes criminal fines up to ten lakh rupees and imprisonment up to two years on manufacturers and service providers who publish false or deceptive advertisements.
89.applicability_notes: Crucial statutory weapon against fake 100% placement guarantees, spurious cosmetic claims, and deceptive finfluencer promotions.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

127.official_section_title: Removal of motor vehicles abandoned or left unattended on a public place
127.official_text: (1) Where any motor vehicle is abandoned, or left unattended, or causing impediment to the free flow of traffic, on a public place, the authority having jurisdiction under this Act may cause such vehicle to be towed away or removed by a towing service or by any other suitable means. (2) Where an abandoned, unattended, or illegally parked vehicle is removed by a towing service under sub-section (1), that service shall bear the responsibility for any loss or damage caused to the motor vehicle during such removal or impoundment.
127.simplified_explanation: Regulates the towing of vehicles parked unlawfully or causing traffic impediment. Explicitly makes towing agencies and authorities responsible for any physical damage caused to the vehicle during towing.
127.applicability_notes: Protects citizens when their vehicle is towed unlawfully (e.g. while occupants are inside, or without public notice) or when the vehicle is damaged during the towing process.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

130.official_section_title: Duty to produce licence and certificate of registration
130.official_text: (1) The driver of a motor vehicle in any public place shall, on demand by any police officer in uniform, produce his licence for examination... (2) The conductor, if any, of a motor vehicle on any public place shall, on demand by any officer of the Motor Vehicles Department authorised in this behalf, produce the certificate of registration of the vehicle and where the vehicle is a transport vehicle, the certificate of fitness and the permit...
130.simplified_explanation: Governs an officer's authority to inspect driving licences and vehicle registration. Under government rules and advisories, presenting documents in electronic form (DigiLocker / mParivahan) satisfies this requirement.
130.applicability_notes: Directly relevant when traffic police stop a vehicle and demand physical documents, refusing to accept verified electronic credentials.

185.official_section_title: Driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs
185.official_text: Whoever, while driving, or attempting to drive, a motor vehicle— (a) has, in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. of blood detected in a test by a breath analyser, or in any other test including a laboratory test... shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine of ten thousand rupees, or with both...
185.simplified_explanation: Defines driving under the influence of alcohol (BAC exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected via breath analyser) with penalties of fine and court prosecution.
185.applicability_notes: Establishes the objective statutory limit and device requirement; protects citizens against arbitrary detention where breath analyser testing is refused or conducted improperly.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

190_2.official_section_title: Violation of standards relating to road safety, pollution, etc.
190_2.official_text: Any person who drives or causes or allows to be driven, in any public place a motor vehicle, which violates the standards prescribed in relation to road safety, control of noise and air-pollution, shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both and he shall be disqualified for holding licence for a period of three months.
190_2.simplified_explanation: Imposes penalties for driving a vehicle that violates air pollution standards (missing or expired Pollution Under Control - PUC certificate).
190_2.applicability_notes: Relevant when an officer fines a driver for PUC violations; online verified PUC on Parivahan satisfies this requirement without needing physical paper slips.

194b.official_section_title: Use of safety belts and the seating of children
194b.official_text: (1) Whoever drives a motor vehicle without wearing a safety belt or carries passengers not wearing safety belts shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees... (2) Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven with a child under twelve years of age not secured by safety belt or child restraint system shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees.
194b.simplified_explanation: Specifies mandatory wearing of seat belts by driver and front/rear passengers, with a statutory compounding fine of one thousand rupees.
194b.applicability_notes: Relevant for disputed e-challans where photographic camera evidence incorrectly records an obstruction or garment strap as an unfastened seatbelt.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

194d.official_section_title: Penalty for not wearing protective headgear
194d.official_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven in contravention of the provisions of section 129 or the rules or regulations made thereunder shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees and he shall be disqualified for holding licence for a period of three months.
194d.simplified_explanation: Mandates wearing of BIS-certified protective helmets by two-wheeler riders and pillions, with a fine of one thousand rupees and 3-month licence disqualification.
194d.applicability_notes: Applicable when contesting erroneous automated camera challans that fail to detect certified helmets due to bad lighting, turbans, or passenger occlusions.

200.official_text: (1) Any offence punishable under section 177, section 178, section 179, section 180, section 181, section 182, sub-section (1) or sub-section (3) or sub-section (4) of section 183, section 184, section 186, section 189, sub-section (2) of section 190, section 192, section 194, section 196 or section 198, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded by such officers or authorities and for such amount as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify in this behalf.
200.simplified_explanation: Provides for compounding (settlement by paying an official fine) of minor traffic offences. Payment must be made only to notified officers with an official receipt or through digital challan systems.
200.applicability_notes: Clarifies that compounding requires an official government notification and receipt; officers cannot demand arbitrary unreceipted cash payments on the spot.

203.official_text: (1) A police officer in uniform or an officer of the Motor Vehicles Department may require any person driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle in a public place to provide one or more specimens of breath for breath test there or nearby, if the officer has reasonable cause to suspect him of having alcohol in his body... (6) If a person required by a police officer under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) to provide a specimen of breath for a breath test refuses or fails to do so and the officer has reasonable cause to suspect him of having alcohol in his body, the officer may arrest him without warrant...
203.simplified_explanation: Outlines the lawful procedure for conducting roadside breath analyser tests and specifies when an officer can request a specimen of breath.
203.applicability_notes: Regulates drunk driving roadside checkpoints; mandates the use of an approved testing device rather than personal subjective smelling.

206.official_section_title: Power of police officer to impound document
206.official_text: (1) Any police officer or other person authorised in this behalf by the State Government may, if he has reason to believe that any identification mark on a motor vehicle is false, or that the certificate of registration, permit, or licence produced to him by the driver or person in charge of the vehicle is false, seize the mark or document and call upon the driver or person in charge to surrender the same. (2) Any police officer or other person authorised in this behalf by the State Government may, if he has reason to believe that the driver of a motor vehicle who is charged with any offence under this Act may abscond or otherwise avoid the service of a summons, seize any licence held by such driver and forward it to the court taking cognizance of the offence and the said court shall on the first appearance of such driver, if the licence has not already been returned to him, return the licence to him in exchange for the temporary acknowledgment given of its seizure...
206.simplified_explanation: Strictly limits when an officer can impound physical documents: only for suspected forgery or risk of absconding, and mandates issuing an official temporary acknowledgment.
206.applicability_notes: Key protection when an officer arbitrarily seizes an original driving licence or registration certificate without issuing an official seizure memo or receipt.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

207.official_section_title: Power to detain vehicles used without certificate of registration, permit, etc.
207.official_text: (1) Any police officer or other person authorised in this behalf by the State Government may, if he has reason to believe that a motor vehicle has been or is being used in contravention of the provisions of section 3 or section 4 or section 39 or without the permit required by sub-section (1) of section 66 or in contravention of any condition of such permit relating to the route on which or the area in which or the purpose for which the vehicle may be used, seize and detain the vehicle, in the prescribed manner and for this purpose take or cause to be taken any steps he may consider proper for the temporary safe custody of the vehicle...
207.simplified_explanation: Authorizes vehicle detention ONLY for specific serious statutory violations (driving without licence, unregistered vehicle, or severe permit violations), requiring prescribed custody procedures.
207.applicability_notes: Protects drivers when traffic personnel unlawfully snatch ignition keys or detain vehicles for minor non-detainable violations like missing pollution certificates or lane indiscipline.

208.official_text: (1) The court taking cognizance of any offence (other than an offence punishable with imprisonment) under this Act may state upon the summons to be served on the accused person that he— (a) may appear by pleader and not in person; or (b) may, by a specified date prior to the hearing of the charge, plead guilty to the charge and remit to the court, by money order, such sum not exceeding the maximum fine that may be imposed for the offence...
208.simplified_explanation: Provides the statutory framework for summary disposal and contestation of traffic challans in virtual or physical courts without requiring lengthy trial appearances.
208.applicability_notes: Directly relevant when a citizen disputes a wrongful challan and chooses to have the matter heard before a Virtual Court or regular Magistrate.

112.official_text: (1) No person shall drive a motor vehicle or cause or allow a motor vehicle to be driven in any public place at a speed exceeding the maximum speed or below the minimum speed fixed for the vehicle under this Act or by or under any other law for the time being in force... (2) The State Government or any authority authorised in this behalf by the State Government may, if satisfied that it is necessary to do so in the interest of public safety or convenience... fix by notification in the Official Gazette speed limits for motor vehicles...
112.simplified_explanation: Governs the determination and enforcement of legal speed limits on public roads. Speed limits must be duly notified and clearly displayed by official traffic signs.
112.applicability_notes: Essential when challenging speed camera challans generated where official speed limit signboards were absent, contradictory, or where camera calibration is disputed.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

47.official_section_title: Assignment of new registration mark on removal to another State
47.official_text: (1) When a motor vehicle not being a transport vehicle has been kept in another State for a period exceeding twelve months, the owner or other person in charge of the vehicle shall apply to the registering authority within whose jurisdiction the vehicle then is, for the assignment of a new registration mark... Provided that an application under this sub-section shall be made within thirty days from the date of expiry of the period of twelve months...
47.simplified_explanation: Grants private vehicle owners the legal right to keep and drive their out-of-state registered vehicle in another state for up to 12 months without requiring new registration or re-registration.
47.applicability_notes: Directly protects citizens from arbitrary harassment and unlawful seizure by local traffic police for driving out-of-state vehicles during visits, temporary employment, or road trips under 12 months.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

114.official_text: (1) Any officer of the Motor Vehicles Department authorised in this behalf by the State Government or any police officer authorised in this behalf by the State Government may, if he has reason to believe that a goods vehicle or trailer is being used in contravention of section 113, require the driver for the purpose of weighing the vehicle to drive it to a weighbridge or other weighing device... and the driver of any such vehicle who fails to comply with any such requisition shall be punishable...
114.simplified_explanation: Authorizes officers to weigh vehicles suspected of overloading on an approved weighbridge or weighing device. Mandates that visual estimation cannot substitute for an objective weighbridge measurement.
114.applicability_notes: Protects transport drivers when enforcement personnel issue arbitrary overloading challans without actually taking the vehicle to a certified government weighbridge.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

116.official_text: (1) The State Government or any authority authorised in this behalf by the State Government may cause or permit traffic signs to be placed or erected in any public place for the purpose of bringing to public knowledge any speed limits fixed under sub-section (2) of section 112 or any prohibitions or restrictions imposed under section 115, or generally for the purpose of regulating motor vehicle traffic... (3) Traffic signs specified in the Schedule shall be of the size, colour and type specified therein...
116.simplified_explanation: Places a legal duty on road authorities to place and maintain clear, standardized traffic signboards for speed limits, no-entry zones, and one-way streets.
116.applicability_notes: Essential defense when challenging automated camera or police challans for 'No Entry' or 'Speeding' where signboards were missing, vandalized, or obscured by foliage.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

177.official_section_title: General provision for punishment of offences
177.official_text: Whoever contravenes any provision of this Act or of any rule, regulation or notification made thereunder, for which no special penalty is provided for the first offence, be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, and for any second or subsequent offence with fine which may extend to one thousand and five hundred rupees.
177.simplified_explanation: The general penalty provision for minor procedural traffic infractions (such as minor stop-line breaches or missing documentation) where no specific major fine is stipulated.
177.applicability_notes: Limits the maximum fine traffic police can demand for minor non-scheduled road infractions to five hundred rupees for a first offence.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

194.official_text: (1) Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven in contravention of the provisions of section 113 or section 114 or section 115 shall be punishable with a minimum fine of twenty thousand rupees and an additional fine of two thousand rupees per tonne of excess load, together with the liability to pay charges for off-loading the excess load...
194.simplified_explanation: Specifies heavy statutory fines for driving a vehicle exceeding permissible axle or gross vehicle weight, requiring certified weighing and off-loading of excess cargo.
194.applicability_notes: Directly relevant for commercial transport disputes regarding whether statutory overloading penalties were lawfully calculated based on actual weighbridge slips.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

129.official_text: Every person, above four years of age, driving or riding or being carried on a motorcycle of any class or description shall, while in a public place, wear protective headgear conforming to such standards as may be prescribed by the Central Government: Provided that the provisions of this section shall not apply to a person who is a Sikh, if he is, while driving or riding on the motorcycle, in a public place, wearing a turban...
129.simplified_explanation: Mandates that both the two-wheeler rider and the pillion passenger wear BIS-certified protective helmets, with statutory exemption for Sikhs wearing a turban.
129.applicability_notes: Statutory basis for helmet compliance and for challenging unlawful fines when riders are wearing ISI/BIS certified helmets or qualify for turban exemptions.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

134.official_section_title: Duty of driver in case of accident and injury to a person
134.official_text: When any person is injured or any property of a third party is damaged, as a result of an accident in which a motor vehicle is involved, the driver of the vehicle or other person in charge of the vehicle shall— (a) take all reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured person... and it shall be the duty of every registered medical practitioner or the doctor on duty... immediately to attend on the injured person and render medical aid or treatment without waiting for any procedural formalities... (b) give on demand by a police officer any information required by him... (c) report to the insurer...
134.simplified_explanation: Sets out the legal duty to provide immediate medical attention to road accident victims and statutory protection ensuring hospitals treat victims immediately without procedural delays.
134.applicability_notes: Underpins Good Samaritan rights and hospital duties to provide emergency trauma care without demanding police clearance or registration fees.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

184.official_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner which is dangerous to the public, having regard to all the circumstances of the case including the nature, condition and use of the place where the vehicle is driven and the amount of traffic which actually is at the time or which might reasonably be expected to be in the place, shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year but which shall not be less than six months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees but which shall not be less than one thousand rupees, or with both...
184.simplified_explanation: Penalizes dangerous driving, jumping red traffic lights, aggressive lane cutting, and mobile phone usage while operating a motor vehicle.
184.applicability_notes: The primary section under which red-light and dangerous driving challans are issued; vital for contesting camera glitches or disputed signal timings.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

192a.official_text: (1) Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven in contravention of the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 66 or in contravention of any condition of a permit relating to the route on which or the area in which or the purpose for which the vehicle may be used, shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, but which shall not be less than five thousand rupees...
192a.simplified_explanation: Penalizes operating a commercial, taxi, or transport vehicle without a valid statutory permit or in violation of permit conditions.
192a.applicability_notes: Relevant for commercial cab drivers, auto operators, and tourist bus operators facing permit seizure or disputed route non-compliance challans.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

196.official_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven in contravention of the provisions of section 146 shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine of two thousand rupees, or with both, and for a subsequent offence with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine of four thousand rupees, or with both.
196.simplified_explanation: Imposes a fine of two thousand rupees or up to three months imprisonment for driving an automobile without mandatory third-party motor insurance.
196.applicability_notes: Applicable when contesting automated or roadside fines issued for 'no insurance' when the vehicle was actively insured but not yet updated on the central Vahan portal.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

3.official_section_title: Prohibition of discrimination on ground of sex
3.official_text: (1) There shall be no discrimination among employees on the ground of sex in matters relating to wages by the same employer, in respect of the same work or work of a similar nature done by any employee. (2) No employer shall,— (i) for the purposes of complying with the provisions of sub-section (1), reduce the rate of wages of any employee; and (ii) make any discrimination on the ground of sex against employees in recruitment for the same work or work of similar nature...
3.simplified_explanation: Strictly prohibits wage discrimination on the ground of sex or gender for the same work or work of a similar nature.
3.applicability_notes: Directly applies where female workers or employees are paid lower wages or salaries than male colleagues doing the same work.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

6.official_text: (1) Subject to the provisions of section 9, the appropriate Government shall fix the minimum rates of wages payable to employees in accordance with the provisions of section 8. (2) For the purpose of sub-section (1), the appropriate Government shall fix a minimum rate of wages— (a) for time work; or (b) for piece work...
6.simplified_explanation: Mandates that the appropriate government fix statutory minimum wage rates that employers are legally obligated to pay without exception.
6.applicability_notes: Governs situations where workers or employees are paid less than the legally mandated minimum floor wage or state minimum wage rates.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

14.official_text: Where an employee whose minimum rate of wages has been fixed under this Code by the day, or by such other period as may be prescribed, works on any day in excess of the number of hours constituting a normal working day, the employer shall pay him for every hour or for part of an hour so worked in excess, at the overtime rate which shall not be less than twice the normal rate of wages.
14.simplified_explanation: Requires employers to pay overtime wages at not less than twice the normal wage rate for any hours worked beyond normal working hours.
14.applicability_notes: Direct statutory remedy when an employer forces employees to work extended hours, weekends, or shifts without mandatory double-rate overtime pay.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

17.official_section_title: Time limit for payment of wages
17.official_text: (1) The employer shall pay or cause to be paid wages to the employees, engaged on— (a) daily basis, at the end of the shift; (b) weekly basis, on the last working day of the week, that is to say, before the weekly holiday; (c) fortnightly basis, before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight; (d) monthly basis, before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month. (2) Where an employee has been— (i) removed, or dismissed from service; or (ii) retrenched or has resigned from service, or became unemployed due to closure of the establishment, the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or, as the case may be, his resignation.
17.simplified_explanation: Strictly mandates wage payment deadlines (e.g. before the 7th of every month) and requires full and final wage settlement within two working days of resignation, removal, or termination.
17.applicability_notes: Primary section for delayed salary payments and for employers withholding full and final settlement (F&F) after an employee resigns or is terminated.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

18.official_section_title: Deductions which may be made from wages
18.official_text: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, there shall be no deductions from the wages of the employee, except those authorised under this Code. (2) Deductions from the wages of an employee shall be made only in accordance with the provisions of this Code, and may be made only for the following purposes, namely:— (a) fines; (b) deductions for absence from duty; (c) deductions for damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to the employee...
18.simplified_explanation: Prohibits all unauthorized deductions from salary. Deductions can only be made for legally specified reasons (such as statutory PF/tax, proven absent days, or authorized recovery) subject to legal ceilings.
18.applicability_notes: Protects employees against arbitrary salary cuts, unilateral notice-period penalty deductions, unverified performance penalties, or failure to deposit PF.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

45.official_section_title: Claims under Code and procedure thereof
45.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint one or more authorities, not below the rank of a Gazetted Officer, to hear and determine the claims which arises under the provisions of this Code. (2) The authority appointed under sub-section (1), while deciding the claim under that sub-section, may order, having regard to the circumstances under which the claim arises, the payment of compensation in addition to the claim determined, which may extend, in the case of minimum wages, to ten times of the amount of such claim...
45.simplified_explanation: Empowers designated Labour Authorities to hear worker wage claims and award compensation of up to ten times the unpaid or delayed amount in addition to the wages owed.
45.applicability_notes: The formal statutory dispute resolution route for recovery of unpaid wages, illegal deductions, and minimum wage shortfalls through Labour Commissioners and the Samadhan portal.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

13.official_section_title: Number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day
13.official_text: (1) Where the minimum rates of wages have been fixed under this Code, the appropriate Government may— (a) fix the number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day inclusive of one or more specified intervals; (b) provide for a day of rest in every period of seven days which shall be allowed to all employees or to any specified class of employees and for the payment of remuneration in respect of such days of rest...
13.simplified_explanation: Mandates that normal working days cannot exceed statutory daily hour limits (8-9 hours) and legally guarantees a mandatory paid day of rest (weekly holiday) every seven days.
13.applicability_notes: Directly protects contract workers, security guards, and shift employees forced to work 7 days a week continuously without a mandatory weekly day off.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

9.official_section_title: Power of Central Government to fix floor wage
9.official_text: (1) The Central Government may, after taking into account the minimum living standards of a worker, fix floor wage: Provided that different floor wages may be fixed for different geographical areas. (2) The minimum rates of wages fixed by the appropriate Government under section 6 shall not be less than the floor wage and if the minimum rates of wages fixed by the appropriate Government in respect of any employment are less than the floor wage, they shall not be reduced by the appropriate Government.
9.simplified_explanation: Empowers the Central Government to establish a statutory national floor wage below which no state or employer is legally permitted to pay any employee.
9.applicability_notes: Protects outsourced data processors, remote gig workers, and low-wage workers against predatory employer wage fixing below national baseline levels.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

26.official_text: (1) There shall be paid to every employee, drawing wages not exceeding such amount per mensem as may be determined by notification, by the appropriate Government, by his employer, who has worked for not less than thirty days in an accounting year, an annual minimum bonus calculated at the rate of eight and one-third per cent of the wages earned by the employee or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher, whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in the accounting year...
26.simplified_explanation: Mandates that every employee who has worked at least thirty days in an accounting year is legally entitled to an annual minimum bonus of 8.33% of wages.
26.applicability_notes: Statutory guarantee for employees whose employers arbitrarily withhold annual bonus payments claiming zero company profits.
keywords: eight and one third per cent

50.official_text: (1) Every employer of an establishment to which this Code applies shall maintain a register containing the details of the persons employed, muster roll, wages and such other details in such manner as may be prescribed. (2) Every employer shall display a notice on the notice board... (3) Every employer shall issue wage slips to the employees in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
50.simplified_explanation: Obligates employers to maintain statutory employment records, muster rolls, and to issue written wage slips specifying salary components and deductions to all workers.
50.applicability_notes: Direct basis for action against establishments that pay cash without payslips or conceal wage deductions and overtime hours.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

51.official_section_title: Appointment of Inspector-cum-Facilitators and their powers
51.official_text: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint Inspector-cum-Facilitators for the purposes of this Code... (3) Every Inspector-cum-Facilitator shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code... (4) The Inspector-cum-Facilitator may— (a) advise employers and workers relating to compliance with the provisions of this Code; (b) inspect the establishment as assigned to him; (c) examine any person found in any premises...
51.simplified_explanation: Authorizes statutory labour Inspector-cum-Facilitators to inspect workplaces, examine employer wage records, and investigate non-compliance with wage laws.
51.applicability_notes: Provides the statutory mechanism for workers to demand formal government labour inspections when companies refuse to rectify wage theft.

15.official_text: "Coercion" is the committing, or threatening to commit, any act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code, or the unlawful detaining, or threatening to detain, any property, to the prejudice of any person whatever, with the intention of causing any person to enter into an agreement.
15.simplified_explanation: Defines coercion as forcing someone to sign an agreement or settlement by unlawful detention of property or threats of unlawful acts.
15.applicability_notes: Applies when a citizen or vendor is forced to sign an unfair settlement, waiver, or release deed under threats or unlawful withholding of their assets.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

19.official_section_title: Voidability of agreements without free consent
19.official_text: When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
19.simplified_explanation: Gives the victim the legal right to cancel and invalidate any contract or agreement that they were tricked, coerced, or defrauded into signing.
19.applicability_notes: Enables citizens to rescind contracts entered into based on false misrepresentations or signed under financial duress.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

27.official_section_title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
27.official_text: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void.
27.simplified_explanation: Declares that any agreement or contract clause that restricts a person from practicing their lawful profession, trade, or business (such as post-employment non-compete clauses) is legally VOID and unenforceable in India.
27.applicability_notes: Key statutory defense for employees, consultants, and freelancers threatened with legal action under post-employment non-compete agreements.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

37.official_text: The parties to a contract must either perform, or offer to perform, their respective promises, unless such performance is dispensed with or excused under the provisions of this Act, or of any other law.
37.simplified_explanation: Establishes the fundamental legal obligation that both parties who enter into an agreement must fulfill their agreed contractual promises.
37.applicability_notes: Foundation for any dispute where one party simply refuses to carry out agreed tasks, deliver goods, or return property as promised.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

39.official_section_title: Effect of refusal of party to perform promise wholly
39.official_text: When a party to a contract has refused to perform, or disabled himself from performing, his promise in its entirety, the promisee may put an end to the contract, unless he has signified, by words or conduct, his acquiescence in its continuance.
39.simplified_explanation: Allows a party to terminate the contract when the other party completely refuses to perform or makes it impossible to fulfill their obligations.
39.applicability_notes: Applies when a contractor, vendor, or service provider abandons the project or announces they will not complete agreed work.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

70.official_section_title: Obligation of person enjoying benefit of non-gratuitous act
70.official_text: Where a person lawfully does anything for another person, or delivers anything to him, not intending to do so gratuitously, and such other person enjoys the benefit thereof, the latter is bound to make compensation to the former in respect of, or to restore, the thing so done or delivered.
70.simplified_explanation: Mandates that when someone performs work or delivers services/goods for another person without intending it as free/charity, and the recipient enjoys the benefit, the recipient is legally bound to pay fair compensation.
70.applicability_notes: Crucial statutory provision for freelance professionals, designers, software developers, and small vendors whose delivered work was accepted and used but never paid for.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

73.official_section_title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
73.official_text: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it.
73.simplified_explanation: Entitles the aggrieved party to financial compensation and damages for direct monetary losses resulting from a breach of contract.
73.applicability_notes: Primary remedy for financial recovery in breach of contract cases, withheld security deposits, and contractor defaults.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

74.official_section_title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
74.official_text: When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for.
74.simplified_explanation: Prevents unfair or extortionate penalty clauses and unreasonable forfeiture of advance deposits, limiting compensation strictly to reasonable proven damages.
74.applicability_notes: Directly applies where vendors, sellers, or builders attempt to forfeit 100% of large advance deposits under harsh penalty clauses.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

75.official_section_title: Party rightfully rescinding contract, entitled to compensation
75.official_text: A person who rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for any damage which he has sustained through the non-fulfilment of the contract.
75.simplified_explanation: Clarifies that when an innocent party rightfully cancels an agreement due to the other party's breach or failure, they retain the legal right to claim compensation for all losses suffered.
75.applicability_notes: Directly supports claims where a citizen cancels a contract because the other party failed to deliver, and seeks reimbursement of advances and consequential losses.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

56.official_text: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.
56.simplified_explanation: Declares that a contract becomes void if unforeseen supervening events (natural disasters, severe medical emergencies, government prohibitions) make performance physically impossible (Doctrine of Frustration).
56.applicability_notes: Protects parties from penalty clauses and breach claims when events entirely beyond their control (pandemics, floods, sudden incapacitation) prevent fulfilling contractual dates.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

65.official_section_title: Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void
65.official_text: When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it, to the person from whom he received it.
65.simplified_explanation: Mandates that when a contract is cancelled, frustrated, or becomes void, any person who took advance payments or benefits must refund or restore those benefits to the other party.
65.applicability_notes: Direct legal basis for compelling banquet halls, event organizers, or vendors to refund advance deposits when an event is cancelled due to impossibility or frustration.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

18.official_text: "Misrepresentation" means and includes— (1) the positive assertion, in a manner not warranted by the information of the person making it, of that which is not true, though he believes it to be true; (2) any breach of duty which, without an intent to deceive, gains an advantage to the person committing it... by misleading another to his prejudice... (3) causing, however innocently, a party to an agreement, to make a mistake as to the substance of the thing which is the subject of the agreement.
18.simplified_explanation: Defines misrepresentation: making untrue assertions or misleading statements regarding the core subject of an agreement, even without deliberate criminal intent.
18.applicability_notes: Key statutory basis when an investor, buyer, or franchisee enters into an agreement based on false figures, fabricated profit claims, or misleading business representations.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

16.official_text: (1) A contract is said to be induced by 'undue influence' where the relations subsisting between the parties are such that one of the parties is in a position to dominate the will of the other and uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage over the other. (2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing principle, a person is deemed to be in a position to dominate the will of another— (a) where he holds a real or apparent authority over the other, or where he stands in a fiduciary relation to the other; or (b) where he makes a contract with a person whose mental capacity is temporarily or permanently affected by reason of age, illness, or mental or bodily distress.
16.simplified_explanation: Defines undue influence where one party exploits a position of dominant authority, trust, or another's vulnerability (such as old age or distress) to extract an unfair contract.
16.applicability_notes: Ground for voiding unconscionable agreements signed by vulnerable senior citizens, dependent tenants, or distressed borrowers under dominant pressure.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

17.official_text: 'Fraud' means and includes any of the following acts committed by a party to a contract, or with his connivance, or by his agent, with intent to deceive another party thereto or his agent, or to induce him to enter into the contract:— (1) the suggestion, as a fact, of that which is not true, by one who does not believe it to be true; (2) the active concealment of a fact by one having knowledge or belief of the fact; (3) a promise made without any intention of performing it; (4) any other act fitted to deceive; (5) any such act or omission as the law specially declares to be fraudulent.
17.simplified_explanation: Defines contractual fraud: active concealment of defects, deliberate falsehoods, or making promises with zero intention of fulfilling them to induce an agreement.
17.applicability_notes: Legal foundation to cancel agreements and recover damages when sellers or commercial partners deliberately hide major structural defects or financial liabilities.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

23.official_section_title: What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not
23.official_text: The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless— it is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.
23.simplified_explanation: Declares that any agreement whose purpose or consideration violates statutory law, is fraudulent, causes injury, or opposes public policy is completely void from the beginning.
23.applicability_notes: Nullifies illegal contract clauses, predatory loan penalties, and unlawful employer bond agreements that contradict public statutes.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

28.official_section_title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
28.official_text: Every agreement— (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to that extent.
28.simplified_explanation: Renders completely void any contractual clause that bars a party from approaching courts/tribunals or artificially shortens statutory limitation periods.
28.applicability_notes: Protects consumers, contractors, and employees from oppressive clauses claiming 'neither party shall approach any court or forum for redressal'.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)

124.official_text: A contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself, or by the conduct of any other person, is called a 'contract of indemnity'.
124.simplified_explanation: Defines an indemnity contract where one party legally promises to protect and reimburse the other against losses caused by their own actions or third parties.
124.applicability_notes: Underpins commercial vendor agreements, service-level guarantees, and IP liability protection disputes between businesses and contractors.

verification.verified_by: Legal Knowledge Base Admin (Verified from India Code)
